title: Cartier part along one prescribed integral divisor
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $D\hookrightarrow X$ be an integral effective Cartier divisor, with ideal $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal K)\subseteq |D|$, where support is the set of points with nonzero stalk. The generic point $\eta$ of $D$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\eta}=1$. There is an integer $a\geq0$ such that $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L^a$ and, at $\eta$, $\mathcal K_\eta=\mathcal L_\eta^a$. The support of $\mathcal L^a/\mathcal K$ is contained in a closed subset $T\subseteq |D|$ every irreducible component of which has codimension at least $2$ in $X$. Here $\mathcal L^a$ denotes the ordinary ideal power [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]; the codimension of an irreducible closed subset is the dimension of the local ring at its generic point [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 0AGB (divisors-lemma-codim-1-part), singleton family D and empty Z-prime; generic-stalk equality is explicit in its proof.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_X/\mathcal K$. The cokernel-closure theorem makes $\mathcal Q$ quasi-coherent; it is of finite type since its local sections are generated as a sheaf by the image of $1$. Thus the locally Noetherian coherence criterion makes it coherent. Apply the support-annihilation theorem to $\mathcal Q$ and the ideal $\mathcal L$: its zero set is $|D|$ by the affine closed-immersion description. The assumed support inclusion gives some $N\geq0$ with $\mathcal L^N\mathcal Q=0$, equivalently $\mathcal L^N\subseteq\mathcal K$. This includes $N=0$, when $\mathcal K=\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 0AGB (lemma-codim-1-part), choice of finite generic valuations; coherent.tex Tag 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf) verifies their finiteness.

proof.text: Choose an affine Cartier chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ meeting $D$, with $\mathcal L(U)=(f)$ and multiplication by $f$ injective. The affine-open Noetherian theorem gives that $A$ is Noetherian. By the closed-immersion ideal description, $D\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f))$; this is a nonempty affine open of the integral scheme $D$, so $A/(f)$ is a domain. Hence $(f)$ is prime and its point is $\eta$. The affine module-germ localization theorem, applied to $\mathcal O_X$ and to $\mathcal L$, identifies $R=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ with $A_{(f)}$ and $\mathcal L_\eta$ with $fR$. The regular principal-prime localization theorem makes $R$ a DVR. The localization-at-prime definition identifies its maximal ideal with $(f)R$, so $\pi=f/1$ is a uniformizer. In particular $\dim R=1$ by the DVR dimension theorem.

Step 1 gives $\pi^N R\subseteq\mathcal K_\eta$. Since $R$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$, this ideal is nonzero. By the definition of a DVR it is principal, say $\mathcal K_\eta=bR$ with $b\ne0$. Also $R$ is Noetherian: every ideal is principal and therefore finitely generated. Apply the unit-times-uniformizer-power theorem to write $b=u\pi^a$, with $u$ a unit and $a\geq0$. Consequently $\mathcal K_\eta=\pi^aR=\mathcal L_\eta^a$. This equality is intrinsic: changing the local equation multiplies $\pi$ by a unit and leaves its power ideal unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, first paragraph: minimal valuation in the ideal at the generic DVR; algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion.

proof.text: On any affine Cartier chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ meeting $D$, write $I=\mathcal K(U)$ and $\mathcal L(U)=(f)$. As in step 2, $(f)$ is prime and $f$ is a nonzerodivisor. The affine module-germ localization theorem and step 3 give $IA_{(f)}=f^aA_{(f)}$. For $h\in I$, clearing the denominator and the localization equality gives $sh=f^ab$ in $A$ for some $s\notin(f)$ and $b\in A$: if the equality of fractions initially needs a further multiplier outside $(f)$, multiply both $s$ and $b$ by it. Prove by induction on $a$ that this implies $h\in(f^a)$. The case $a=0$ is immediate. For $a>0$, primeness of $(f)$ and $s\notin(f)$ give $h=fh_1$. Cancelling the nonzerodivisor $f$ gives $sh_1=f^{a-1}b$, so induction applies. Thus $I\subseteq(f^a)$. The quasi-coherent affine descriptions of $\mathcal K$ and the ideal powers give $\mathcal K|_U\subseteq\mathcal L^a|_U$.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, proof of the claim: injectivity modulo powers of one prime local equation; the singleton case needs only this elementary prime-power induction.

proof.text: At $x\notin|D|$, the affine closed-immersion description gives $\mathcal L_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The support hypothesis gives $\mathcal K_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ as well: the stalk of the quotient is the quotient of the stalk ideals. Thus the inclusion is automatic off $D$. Together with step 4 on Cartier charts this proves $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L^a$ on all of $X$. Equality of subsheaves can be checked on stalks: a section whose germs lie in a subsheaf has local lifts, and these glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, conclusion of the local containment claim.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F=\mathcal L^a/\mathcal K$. The ideal powers are quasi-coherent, so the cokernel-closure theorem makes $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent. Locally $\mathcal L^a=(f^a)$, hence the image of $f^a$ generates the quotient as a sheaf; off $D$ the quotient is zero. Thus $\mathcal F$ is of finite type. The finite-type support theorem shows that $T=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is closed in $X$. Here the quotient stalk is $\mathcal L_x^a/\mathcal K_x$: a germ of a quotient section lifts locally to a section of $\mathcal L^a$, and its germ is zero exactly when, on a smaller neighbourhood, that section lies in $\mathcal K$. This follows directly from the sheaf quotient and germ equivalence relations. Step 5 gives $T\subseteq|D|$, and step 3 gives $\eta\notin T$. We may take this actual support as the closed subset requested in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, last sentence before the final UFD paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), part (1), supplies the closed remainder.

proof.text: Let $C$ be any irreducible component of $T$. It is closed in $X$, and the scheme sobriety theorem supplies its generic point $y$. Since $T\subseteq|D|$ and $\eta\notin T$, $y$ is a strict specialization of $\eta$. By step 2 and the stalk-dimension chain formula, $\eta$ has a strict generalization $z$ (the supremum of the integer chain lengths is $1$). The concatenated chain $y,\eta,z$ consists of two strict generalizations. Therefore the same chain formula gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}\geq2$. This is precisely the codimension of $C$ required in the statement. If $T$ is empty the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, equality at the generic divisor point and the codimension-two conclusion; properties.tex Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring).

Steps: (1) quasi-coherent cokernel, coherence by qc+ft and support-power-ideal-kills give L^N⊆K, which makes the generic ideal nonzero; (2) a Noetherian chart with (f) prime and germ localization give R=A_(f), which is a DVR by the regular-principal-prime node (no domain hypothesis needed), so dim R=1; (3) K_η=bR, b=uπ^a, so K_η=L_η^a; (4) an elementary prime-power induction with cancellation by a nonzerodivisor gives I⊆(f^a); (5) the inclusion holds trivially off D and is checked on stalks; (6) F=L^a/K is qc of finite type, so its support T is closed, T⊆D and η∉T; (7) for a component's generic point y, the chain y,η,z gives dim O_{X,y}≥2 without catenarity. Every cited statement was read and its hypotheses match, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. Edge cases: K=O_X, K=L^r, (x²,xy) in k[x,y,z], (x²y,x³) in k[x,y], disconnected non-integral X. Not duplicates: lem-per-surface-codimension-one-cartier-part and lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations, which need regular integral X.
